item.title: Tesla ramps Optimus production at Fremont to hundreds of units per week
item.description: Tesla has substantially accelerated production of Optimus at its Fremont, California facility, scaling from several dozen units weekly in Q2 2026 to hundreds of units weekly as of late Q3/early Q4. Source: TechRepublic (https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-tesla-optimus-robot-production-2027-sales-timeline/)

item.title: Musk targets late 2027 for external Optimus sales, sub-$20,000 long-term cost
item.description: Elon Musk confirmed Tesla's primary target for external customer sales is scheduled for late 2027, prioritizing internal factory deployment first. The long-term target cost remains sub-$20,000 at high-volume scale (1M units/year). Source: TechRepublic (https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-tesla-optimus-robot-production-2027-sales-timeline/)

item.title: Agility Robotics clears SEC step toward becoming first pure-play public humanoid company
item.description: Agility Robotics, creator of the bipedal warehouse humanoid Digit, officially cleared a key SEC procedural step paving the way for its public listing. This positions Agility to become the market's first pure-play publicly traded humanoid robotics company. Sources: The AI Insider (https://theaiinsider.tech/2026/10/14/agility-robotics-clears-sec-step-on-path-to-becoming-publicly-listed-humanoid-robot-company/) | The Motley Fool (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/10/13/the-first-pure-play-humanoid-robot-stock-is-about/)

item.title: Yaskawa Electric targets 2030 commercial humanoid robot launch
item.description: Industrial automation titan Yaskawa Electric announced a commercial humanoid robot launch target of 2030, citing accelerating embodied AI capabilities and surging factory demand for flexible humanoid labor. Source: Digitimes (https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20261014PD202/yaskawa-forecast-2030-launch-demand.html)

item.title: Cologne police seize teleoperated humanoid robot after alleged harassment incident
item.description: Police in Cologne, Germany seized a 1.2-meter humanoid robot operating outside a commercial district following an alleged harassment incident. Authorities launched an investigation into unauthorized remote teleoperation in pedestrian zones, highlighting emerging legal liability and urban zoning questions for consumer robotics. Source: Cologne Police Report Coverage (https://www.instagram.com/p/Deefk8KI0-y/)

item.title: Figure AI retires Figure 02 fleet as next-gen platforms ramp
item.description: Figure AI has completed the operational retirement of its Figure 02 fleet, clearing manufacturing and engineering capacity to accelerate rollout and real-world testing of its next-generation household and industrial platforms. Source: Figure AI (https://www.figure.ai/news/f-02-decommission)
